name: simulate-qcd-gift-boundary
why: Measured reach for the grouped legacy aggregate scalar-QCD gift planner extracted from simulatePlan. Six dedicated block-Q members run in all four equivalence modes and discriminate current-year named-action suppression, annual age-70.5 and death eligibility, indexed independent donor caps, proportional routed-RMD attribution and sorted reallocation, first-ID logical beyond-RMD sources, compatible duplicate physical rows, full-drain cent flooring and sub-cent suppression, multi-year freshness, complete caller prevalidation, logical pro-rata mutation, one runtime identity per ID, deferred character rows and history writes. Hostile delegation tests pin fail-closed source identity, balance and amount validation because behavior-equivalent capture cannot execute those throws.

entries.label: named suppression, annual donor eligibility and per-donor request cap
sorted proportional owner attribution, personal-cap clamp and residual reallocation
first-ID logical source selection, cent-floor drain and one debit intent per ID

anchors.text: const available = sources.reduce((sum, state) => sum + state.balance, 0)

entries.label: left-associated gift total and fresh ordered output
logical live-state snapshot and exact map handoff
whole-plan logical IRA identity normalization, sequential balance and amount validation
entries.note: Validated differential members take the successful seam. The fail-closed throw cannot execute in a behavior-equivalent capture; hostile delegation independently injects wrong logical positions, owner, non-IRA source, stale balance, zero, positive sub-cent, cumulative overdraw and getter-backed identity intents. It proves complete normalization before mutation and that apply never re-reads helper-owned intent objects.

entries.label: sequential shadow-balance advance and immutable scalar record cache
caller-owned history snapshot and donor identity validation
entries.note: The unknown-donor throw is excluded because a behavior-equivalent corpus cannot take a hostile helper seam. Focused delegation injects throwing history property and iterator channels and proves neither reaches the first logical debit/runtime publication.

entries.label: logical pro-rata debit, single runtime identity, deferred character and history writes

measuredProof.method: The blocks corpus and both engine source trees are materialized from immutable Git objects, then captured in default, cashFlow, optimizerProbe, and counterfactual modes. The head tree is pinned to the semantic source commit, which the verifier requires to be an ancestor of the exact current HEAD, and the current HEAD engine source tree must remain byte-identical to that semantic tree. Before any harness module executes, the verifier authenticates this spec against its path-aware clean-filter working-tree blob and the immutable HEAD blob, derives the complete local transitive import closure from committed source, and requires every closure member to match both its pinned HEAD blob and its clean-filter working-tree blob. It then recomputes corpus, captures, byte-identical structural comparison, reach, and all recorded hashes.
measuredProof.scope: The scalar-QCD source extraction changes no captured output in any block member or mode. The helper and caller retain named-request stand-down, donor eligibility and per-person caps, routed-RMD attribution, grouped logical beyond-RMD debits, exact-cent suppression, runtime/deferred-character publication, and ordered history writes. Focused helper and hostile delegation tests independently pin identity, atomicity, defensive rejection, and publication contracts that a byte-identical dump cannot prove.

harnessRepins.reason: Decision D-CASH-PROPERTY-ALIAS made the plan checks refuse any id two rows would publish a value under, so six blocks members (c8, e5, h1, j4, n1, r1) that shared property, debt or policy ids now give each row its own id. No block-O, block-Q or block-Y member this proof measures changed. The pin is advanced so the harness closure still authenticates at HEAD; the corpus, capture, reach and calibration figures in this record were measured with the earlier blob and were not re-measured. This proof's engine-tree check already ties it to its own head source tree, so it verifies only at that tree.

After main at c2d61967 (plan schema v7, #765) was merged into the D-2027-ROLLOVER branch, two block members no longer parsed under the current tree: j1 (spending phases in a couple) now names phasesAgeOf p1, the person listed first, whose age its phases followed and whom the v7 migration names, and which a tree before v7 drops; and v3 (three qualified contracts) names p1 as each annuitant instead of no owner, the primary the ownerless fallback resolved to. No other member changed. Re-measured by the procedure the D-SS-ANALYSIS-EARNINGS-TEST branch used for the same change: run with the blob this record was measured with (7a1507c9bbf8e42f2e465195628bd389951c8025, the last entry's measuredWithBlob; the blob it pinned, df82d4ee7fbeeaa41c43b1811f05ddb161b01268, was never measured) it reproduces this record's figures exactly, and with this blob only the corpus identity moved: the member hash 1613a1fc1616 to 66cff52e468b and the dump hashes; members stay 121 and entries 484. The comparison is still IDENTICAL with 0 entries moved and the reach counts are unchanged.

Main at 6f668e06 merged into the D-SS-ANALYSIS-EARNINGS-TEST branch. The corpus is main's (whose j1 and v3 v7 edits are the branch's, byte for byte) plus the branch's six block-L members, l10 to l15: the worker's excess charged to the family and both partial-month caps (l15's spouse born in January, so her spouse benefit is entitled, and charged, from the worker's first month), a couple member on a living ex's record after the spouse's death, a spouse who died before his claim, and an SSDI onset at full retirement age. No existing member changed. Re-measured by the same procedure as the entries above: run with the blob the last entry pinned (6332be9dcb1ae7b1038d70e5096708192c59ce5a) it reproduces this record's figures exactly, and with this blob only the corpus identity moved: members 121 to 127, entries 484 to 508, the member hash 66cff52e468b to cd492058d9ea and the dump hashes. The comparison is still IDENTICAL with 0 entries moved and the reach counts are unchanged.

historicalRecord.statement: This proof verifies only at its recorded engine trees: head b63271eaed9a0e5cc36db5b525c834b830f5b16d (packages/engine/src at commit 07b3614d4459ae67fa9de31b28c0f09f0b212680) and base 33d9b00d8054b592361e37710c78f99cc01cee65 (packages/engine/src at commit 815a52b25359c4bbaf103efbf69e2a5bf7d65487). It has not been verifiable at main's HEAD since later commits changed packages/engine/src, so HEAD no longer carries the recorded head tree the verifier requires, and re-pinned this spec, so the recorded specMeasurementSha256 no longer matches it. It stands as a historical record of that extraction, not as a check the current engine passes.

readingTheCounts: A member count proves that at least one line in the named range executed. Reach additionally fails on any cold executable whole line in a reached range. JavaScript line coverage cannot distinguish every ternary, nullish or compound-condition operand sharing one physical line, so focused hostile tests must be read alongside the differential proof.
